description: This migration adds a NOT NULL column with no default to public.repositories, an existing table that (per this codebase's own 0001_init.sql) already holds rows — Postgres has no value to put in that column for any existing row, so applying this migration against a populated database fails outright.

required_findings.justification: `add column active_rule_version text not null` supplies no DEFAULT. On any already-populated table, Postgres rejects this outright ('column contains null values') because there is no value to backfill existing rows with — this migration cannot succeed against production data as written. The safe pattern is a DEFAULT (or a nullable column plus a separate backfill-then-constrain step).

explanation: An unambiguous, self-contained migration-safety defect: the migration will fail to apply against any table that already has rows, with no application code or unseen context required to know that — repositories is one of this codebase's oldest, clearly-populated tables.
